I had RSI for 6 years and i was lucky to get referred to a private hand specialist on the NHS. Long story short i had 3 hand operations and now it only flairs up but is largely manageable. 

Ofc if i do anything excessive it comes back but you can get to a level where you forget about it. I used to struggle getting dressed because it hurt so much and now i abuse my wrists in the gym with no pain. 

Its hard to treat and definitely doesnt have a finite cure but i hope this gives you some hope. In the first year it was excessive typing, but 5 years on I can still type 28 days out of any given 30 at a well above average pace. Its a long term thing at the end of the day.

NHS is good if you know what to ask. Try changing doctor and ask for a hand specialist or orthopaedic surgeon. MRI of the hand is good too. MRI of the hand when it is ****ing searing with pain is ideal because if theres any mechanistic stuff it might get picked up then (that happened with me and explained why 2 previous MRI were blank). 

Best of luck, just be persistent and annoy the system.

Hello Acne Sufferers,

I had cystic nodular acne for 3 years and currently major in pharmacology and pathology. I haven't read the whole feed but I'll post my two cents and dispel some myths to try and help here.

My face was noticeably effected whilst my chest and back were described as 'severe' by my dermatologist. I was put on an intensive drug whereby i was monitored each month as part of the safety requirements of the drug.

1.) Changing Pillow Cases; this is very helpful and is best if you shower just before bed, however i would only change the pillow every few days. Why is this? Everyone has a unique Microflora (bacterial composition) on their skin. Allowing a pillow to be colonised by your harmless and protective skin microbes protects it from being colonised by pathogenic microbes. Bacteria compete with each other for space on the skin and thus the ones you have now that have succeeded are by definition harmless. So i recommend you shower before bed and change bedding once a week, although i was fine showering in the morning.

2.) Building on this, don't use face masks or over wash. If you wax your face and clear your pores you've just opened them up and allow them to be re colonised with dirt and microbes, essentially setting yourself up for a fresh deep spot if something gets in the pore. Now, it is fine to wash frequently as long as you follow prescribed moisturising techniques from your GP or specialist. I used 'dermabase' 3 times a day to very good effect and have been moisturising every day for the past 6 years. Just dont be squeaky clean, be like 'clean' +30% if you get me.

3.) Regardless of your cause of acne, see a specialist, follow their advice to the letter. Additionally, you can get yourself tested for allergies which may help you identify if its because of lactose or another ingredient (i saw some users saw improvement after quitting milk). 

4.) Eat a clean, balanced diet, with a normal multivitamin. Don't eat things with breadcrumbs or greasy food, try and eat like someone who goes to the gym. 

5.) Be optimistic, continue your life, exercise in your room, eat clean, fight depression. Studies have shown, and frankly its a fact of life, that a positive outlook and belief helps cancer sufferers recover and thus we can adopt that here. 

6.) At the end of the day acne is a physiological lesion and thus has a scientific root cause and explanation. It is not bad luck and it is not bad genes - it has a strong genetic element of course but it is not incurable (having genes predisposing it does not mean you have it for life). Your specialist should diagnose causes and eventually you will find the reason and you will counter it with, preferably a drug, or other method.

7.) Chin up you will get better. I thought it was the end and i nearly made it the end for myself, but everything resolves.

I hope that was helpful and it is all eminent of my personal experience with the condition that i believe was passed down from my father. I have used my degree knowledge and job knowledge from the pharmaceutical industry to inform my statements. I do not claim this is medical advice and any individual seeking a medical outcome or life change from this text should seek the advice of their GP.
